title: Dating Q&A #1: Leaving the friendzone, Facing rejection, Opening up to girls
summary: First dating Q&A where NH answers viewer questions on confidence, partners who let themselves go, the friend zone, rejection, the 'female dialect', intimidation, fear/respect and serial chasing. His recurring advice: build your identity alone first, know your worth, set firm boundaries, and slow down.
claims: Having no identity protects you from rejection but also guarantees you are never accepted; build your identity first through many uncomfortable hours alone
Each rejection lets you either reshape your identity or accept yourself; reaching self-acceptance lets you stop caring, which paradoxically makes you attractive because desperation is repellent
He was short until a very late growth spurt; the worst part of being short is the resentment it breeds, which damages social interactions
Never let one thing you can't change, like height, talk you out of improving everything else; lifting raises your status as a man
He dislikes socializing but forces himself to talk to people because conversation turns out to be good for mental health
Don't pursue a relationship until you are an almost complete project; women who want to fix broken men tend to be hot messes
At 19 a man has plenty of time; men reach their prime financially, socially and in confidence in their 40s-50s
You have the right to set boundaries on a partner's body, just as she could veto your face tattoo
If a partner gains a lot of weight, frame it as a health or identity concern and ask what is wrong rather than saying she is no longer attractive
Women respond well to strictness; be firm without ultimatums, give space if she gets emotional, then return to the topic
Weakness is a universal turn-off for women, meaning any inability to provide what she wants, emotionally or financially
Reveal your weaknesses slowly; during the first year with his now wife he revealed none of his
Both partners need a secret garden; there are things he will never tell his wife
Tell your partner what upsets you without dumping the childhood trauma behind it; women like open communication
Friendships with women formed before puberty can stay platonic; after sexual maturity both people judge each other as potential partners on first meeting
Many of the strongest couples he knows started as friendships that ignited into romance
Past a certain age a man and woman can rarely be purely friends unless there is a big age gap
People who fall hard and fast should slow their pace and not project fear of abandonment from past rejections onto new partners
His first rejection left him depressed for about two weeks; with repetition rejection stops affecting you
Women communicate mostly in the emotional subtext beneath the words, men mostly consciously and directly
He later learned that three or four girls in his high-school class wanted to date him but he could not read their signals
Learn the female dialect by listening to the emotions under her words; when she brings a problem she wants understanding, not a solution
Men who fall fast usually lack self-worth and fear solitude; a man must learn to spend time alone
Knowing your worth (attractive, intelligent, good job, stable) is confidence, not arrogance, and protects you from manipulative partners
Friendship with a woman has a brief ambiguous window where it can become romance; once it closes it is closed forever, and the man must be the one to jump through
A woman touching your chest or arm is a sign of attraction; every girl who touched him like that wanted more
After years in the friend zone, confess plainly; rejection is a net positive because it frees you, then cut contact
Women calling you intimidating is a hidden compliment; don't try to be less scary, show warmth through conversation: a beast outside, teddy bear inside
He loves the book The Gift of Fear, which teaches women their primal fear instinct is their best friend
Fear in attraction means respect and uncertainty; a woman who does not respect you cannot love you, so keep some mystery
Object to revealing clothes by expressing insecurity and protective concern rather than control; women dislike being controlled but like being protected
He often goes shirtless and his wife does not mind, because men and women process outside attention differently
The thrill of the chase is like crack cocaine to the male brain; committed men must not let flirting start because the libido cannot be stopped once going
Serial chasers should improve how they select partners, spend time alone, and delay sex to build an emotional connection
In his early 20s he slept with girls once and left them, which he is ashamed of; time alone led him to meet his wife
viewer_questions: breaking out of your shell as a short 19-year-old
sharing weaknesses without driving her away
can men and women be just friends
confessing after 4 years in the friend zone
women attracted to men they fear
losing interest after securing the girl
